name: Weekly burst-firing, left frontal lobe, 30 min (Baker-Price & Persinger 2003)
origin: Baker-Price & Persinger, Persinger/Koren lab, Laurentian University
summary: The left-frontal arm of Baker-Price & Persinger 2003, an open-label study of depression after closed head injury: 30 min of 1 uT burst-firing fields over the left frontal region, once a week for 6 weeks. Seven patients were assigned to this arm and three missed the last two or three sessions; the authors reported that depression scores fell as much as in the bilateral-temporal arm. There was no sham arm.
notes: 14 patients with depression after closed head injury got 30 min once a week for 6 weeks. The field came from two small canisters of four solenoids each, held by Velcro over the temporal lobes or the left frontal region. The burst-firing pattern 'was presented once every 3 sec.' and passed to one pair of solenoids (one in each canister) every 0.5 s (Baker-Price 2003 p.3-4 [967-968]). Where the canisters sat on the left frontal region is not said. This program plays two coils at F7 and F3 together, an inference, without the 0.5-s rotation. Each burst is 230 points of 3 ms (690 ms), followed by a 3-s pause. The paper prints 259 values but points to Persinger 2000 for the picture, where the pattern has 230. The burst is rebuilt as this project's rising sweep with the published point duration and length; the point values were never published as numbers, only as a small graph (Persinger 2000 Fig. 2, p.5 [663]). Field: 1 uT; where it was measured is not stated. This program's setting is the peak field 20 mm in front of each coil. No sham arm. Three of the seven left-frontal patients missed the last two or three sessions (p.3 [967]). Self-rated scores in an open series, where improvement over weeks is expected anyway; never repeated outside the lab. Rats given the same weekly field spent about half as much time in the open arms of a plus maze after two sessions (Fitzpatrick & Persinger 2004 p.1). Independent sham-controlled tests of God-Helmet-type fields found no field effect (Granqvist 2005, double-blind; Gendle & McGrath 2012, where the experimenter knew the condition). This was clinical research on diagnosed patients, not a treatment: depression and head injury need a clinician. A head injury raises seizure risk. Not for anyone with epilepsy or a seizure history; stop on headache, nausea or distress.
setting: Seated or reclined, eyes closed, in a quiet room. The study was an outpatient clinical series with depression questionnaires and QEEG before and after.
schedule: 30 min once a week for 6 weeks, then 6 weeks without sessions (the study's follow-up).
source: Baker-Price & Persinger 2003, Percept Mot Skills 96:965 https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/12831278/ ; Baker-Price & Persinger 1996, Percept Mot Skills 83:491 https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/8902023/ ; Fitzpatrick & Persinger 2004, Percept Mot Skills 98:983 (rats, weekly burst-firing) https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/15209315/ ; Persinger, Hoang & Baker-Price 2009, Electromagn Biol Med 28:374 ('once every 3 s for about 0.7 s') https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/20017628/ ; Carniello 2020, PhD thesis, Laurentian University (230-point burst-firing file, 3 ms) https://laurentian.scholaris.ca/items/8c92763c-cd19-4a21-b242-3b572a28ce55 ; Martin & Persinger 2004, Neurosci Lett 366:226 (burst-firing once every 4 s) https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/15276252/ ; Granqvist et al. 2005, Neurosci Lett 379:1 https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/15849873/ ; Gendle & McGrath 2012, Percept Mot Skills 114:217 https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/22582690/
